name: Anvil Gauntlets (forge-gauntlets)
status_values: not_started | in_progress | done | stand_in | pending_human | blocked
decisions: 2026-09-25: weapons come off the hero bodies; each chassis weapon is its own model attached to hand sockets (the user's decision, relayed by the workflow coordinator). Brax keeps bare forearms and hands; the rock forge-gauntlets are the anvil_gauntlets weapon (art/weapons/anvil_gauntlets/).
2026-09-25: no human artist for stage 2; the AI pipeline makes the production mesh at production quality (the user's decision, relayed by the workflow coordinator).

0_concept_reference.notes: The gauntlets are designed on Brax's approved front and turnaround sheet (gauntlet close-ups: basalt segments with lava in every gap, knuckle plates, bronze elbow cuff and hexagonal strap frame ending in a wrist ring).

1_blockout.notes: Brax's stage-1 TRELLIS.2 blockout (s202) gave the gauntlet dimensions (elbow ring, forearm, hand, fingertip reach). SCULPT REFERENCE ONLY.

2_production_mesh.produced_by: AI (Claude), tools/blender/gf_hero/s2_weapon.py + s2_gauntlet.py + s2_texture.py; no human artist
2_production_mesh.notes: Rigid left/right pair, open (concept) and closed-fist variants with identical topology (shared UVs/texture). v2 (polish pass 2026-09-25): built on the s202 blockout's own gauntlet field (plate centres from its lumps, plate tops on its surface, radial scale 1.04-1.10), chunky faceted basalt plates with 1.5 cm glowing seams, hexagonal bronze cuff / band / strap frame with studs, a broad hand core over the wearer's fingers, massive knuckle chunks, faceted rock fingers; tangent normals baked from the scaled blockout gauntlet. Authored in the weapon socket frame (origin palm centre, +Y along the fingers, +Z out of the back of the hand). All pieces closed and manifold.

3_rig.notes: No skin: rigid. GF_Hero_v1 (stage 3, 2026-09-25) has weapon_L / weapon_R exactly at this weapon's authoring frame: the authored T-pose placement equals the rest attach within 1.8e-7, and in glTF each gauntlet exported alone in its grip frame lands on the rig-held gauntlet within 0.9 um as an identity child of the socket node (docs/art/GF_HERO_SKELETON.md section 3). Measured on Brax (reports/stage3/poses.json weapon_limits): a sleeve weapon, so the wrist must stay straight (clean bend 0 deg, twist -100..60 deg clean, +-120 within 2 vertices); the elbow cuff overlaps the elbow joint by 2 cm and presses into the biceps past about 40 deg of elbow flexion (12-17 vertices at 60-100 deg) - end the sleeve about 4 cm before the elbow or flare the cuff to lift that limit. The fist variant goes with the body's fist clench. Stage 5: export the left gauntlet as the offhand node in its own left grip frame.

4_animation.notes: None of its own; open/fist variant swap is driven by the hero's punch clips.

5_export_validate.produced_by: AI (Claude), tools/blender/gf_hero/export_glb.py --weapon anvil_gauntlets (step 'weapon' of run_stage5.py brax); no human step

sockets.root: anvil_gauntlets = the right grip frame; identity child of the hero's weapon_R
sockets.offhand: the left pair (+ muzzle_2), re-parented to weapon_L with an identity transform; its origin = grip_L
sockets.frame: glTF: -Z = along the fingers, +Y = back of the hand, +X = right

5_export_validate.notes: Open + fist variants as separate mesh nodes (anvil_gauntlets_{fist,open}_{R,L}); all four spawn visible and the client hides the pair it does not show, per hand, at the swap frames of the hero sidecar (clip_info.<clip>.weapon_variant). Attached to Brax through the re-imported sockets within 2e-7 m (rest) and 9e-7 m (brax_jab_r f3); each mesh encloses its hand (wrist, palm, knuckle). The armory's gfa_validate counts every mesh, so it reports 15,432 tris > its 8,000 gauntlet_pair budget; the pair shown is 7,716.

user_final_approval.notes: The user's final visual approval (the Hades-II bar); record signed_off_by / signed_off_on here and on the stage.

human_gates.gate: stage 2: the user's visual approval of the AI-made weapon model
stage 5: the user's final visual approval of the shipped weapon (the Hades-II bar)
